moduleCheckRemoteSize.msgDatabaseGrowing:
**Your database is getting larger!** But do not worry, we can address it now. The time before running out of space on the remote storage.

| Measured size | Configured size |
| --- | --- |
| ${estimatedSize} | ${maxSize} |

> [!MORE]-
> If you have been using it for many years, there may be unreferenced chunks - that is, garbage - accumulating in the database. Therefore, we recommend rebuilding everything. It will probably become much smaller.
>
> If the volume of your vault is simply increasing, it is better to rebuild everything after organizing the files. Tabularium does not delete the actual data even if you delete it to speed up the process. It is roughly documented.
>
> If you don't mind the increase, you can increase the notification limit by 100MB. This is the case if you are running it on your own server. However, it is better to rebuild everything from time to time.
>

> [!WARNING]
> If you perform rebuild everything, make sure all devices are synchronised. The plug-in will merge as much as possible, though.

> - 800: Warn if the remote storage size exceeds 800MB.
>   This is recommended if you are using fly.io with 1GB limit or IBM Cloudant.
> - 2000: Warn if the remote storage size exceeds 2GB.

tabularium.help.connect.body:
Open Connection and sign in with your account on the Tabularium server. Choose an existing vault or create a new one, name this device, and enter the vault's passphrase.

An existing vault is fetched to this device first; a new vault is filled from this device's files. To use another vault, choose Sign in again or change vault. Disconnect forgets the connection on this device only; the device stays listed on the server until it is removed there.

Device credentials last 30 days and renew themselves while the device is used.
tabularium.help.connect.title: Connecting and changing vaults
tabularium.help.errors.body:
Credentials no longer valid: the device was removed on the server or its credentials expired. Sign in again.

Encryption settings refused: this device's settings differ from the vault's. Disconnect and connect again.

A rebuild is in progress: wait until the owner ends it on the web.

A note does not synchronise: check the size limit and the excluded files under Sync, and look in the log.

The first synchronisation of a large vault takes a while; keep Obsidian open until the status shows Up to date.
tabularium.help.errors.title: Common problems
tabularium.help.migrate.body:
Tabularium can run beside other sync plug-ins in the same vault: each synchronises with its own server, and they do not share local databases, settings or flag files. To move your notes, connect to the vault on the Tabularium server that already holds them, so this device fetches it; then turn the old plug-in off, or keep it.

If another plug-in also synchronises plug-in folders, exclude ${pluginDir} there: it holds this device's credentials.
tabularium.help.migrate.title: Moving from the old plug-in
tabularium.help.passphrase.body:
Notes are encrypted on each device with the vault's passphrase before they are sent; the server cannot read them. Every device of a vault uses the same passphrase.

The passphrase cannot be recovered. If it is lost, the notes on the server cannot be decrypted; devices that still have the files can create a new vault from them.
tabularium.help.passphrase.title: The vault passphrase
tabularium.help.rebuild.body:
A rebuild replaces the vault on the server with one device's files, for example to clean up old data. The owner authorises the device on the web (Account settings, Vaults and devices, Rebuild vault), then runs Overwrite the server with this device in Maintenance on that device.

Afterwards the vault is locked. Each other device shows Vault locked and must fetch from the server. When all of them have fetched, unlock the vault here or on the web.
tabularium.help.rebuild.title: Rebuilding and unlocking
tabularium.help.status.body:
The status bar shows the connection and counters. Up to date means nothing is waiting. Changes waiting counts files that have not been sent yet; they are sent with the next synchronisation.

When the device is offline, changes are kept and sent once it is back online. A failed synchronisation is explained in the log (Maintenance, Log).

tabularium.migration.done: Tabularium's local data now has names of its own. Synchronisation continues as before.
tabularium.migration.fetching: Tabularium now keeps its local data under names of its own, apart from other sync plug-ins. Fetching this vault from the server once; newer files win and files only on this device are kept.

tabularium.release.0.12.0: Tabularium names throughout the plug-in; large vaults synchronise reliably; misleading version notices removed.
tabularium.release.0.13.0: One web application: home, web notes, Tabularius and administration.
tabularium.release.0.14.0: Share a note or folder as an encrypted link from the file menu.
tabularium.release.0.15.0: Tabularius, the AI clerk, is set up on the web; web notes read like Obsidian.
tabularium.release.0.16.0: The server's settings, including mail for Send to Kindle, are changed on the web.
tabularium.release.0.17.0: Tabularius answers with recipes: a model with its parameters and a prompt, set up by an administrator; conversations can adjust them.
tabularium.release.0.18.0:
New settings page arranged by use: connection, sync, file sorting, Send to Kindle, appearance, maintenance and help.
Built-in help and version history in three languages.
Confirmations say what happens and what it means for other devices.
Upstream entries that do not apply to a Tabularium server are gone: remote configuration, setup URIs and QR codes, onboarding, hidden-file and customisation sync, P2P.
tabularium.release.0.18.1: One Latin vocabulary for the plug-in and the web pages.
tabularium.release.0.18.2: Tabularius answers a new conversation with the recipe chosen before its first message.
tabularium.release.0.19.0: "Sync" in the file menu above "Sorting": sync now, and a note's version history; the setting texts and the history window that were still in English are translated. The server gains scheduled backups and a round of security fixes.
tabularium.release.0.20.0: Tabularius answers read like notes (tables, code, Mermaid diagrams) and take attachments: pictures, text files and PDFs; web search is switched on per conversation. Web notes draws Mermaid diagrams, keeps the vault open when you come back from a citation, and opens linked notes at the top. Shared pages follow the sharer's colours.
tabularium.release.0.21.0: Check broken links (Maintenance → Links, or the command palette) lists links that reach no file and repairs them with the files of the same name; automatic repair can be turned on for one device. Renames in web notes take links along. A share is refreshed only by the device that last saved it, follows renames and is withdrawn when its note is deleted.
tabularium.release.0.22.0: A quieter web interface with depth: the content floats as a sheet beside the sidebar, states are dots, actions are icons with their names in tooltips, large headings are set in a serif. Clerk conversations can be renamed, grouped into projects and archived from each conversation's menu. Web notes show the sync state beside the vault name and can fold the file tree away. Share pages draw Mermaid diagrams; code blocks are highlighted in about sixty languages.
tabularium.release.0.23.0: Selecting text in a note shows a format toolbar, and right-click offers an Insert submenu (tables, code blocks, Mermaid flowcharts, sequence diagrams, mind maps, Gantt charts, formulas, callouts, dividers); each is also a command. Web notes use the same actions and now edit in source, live render or split view, read rendered or as source, and draw $formulas$. Scroll bars are thin throughout the web pages.
tabularium.release.0.23.1: Password managers no longer put their autofill button on the web pages' ordinary fields (the clerk's message box, searches, settings); sign-in and password fields work with them as before.
tabularium.release.0.24.0: Tabularius can use Gemini, DeepSeek and a local Ollama as model providers. Each account can keep several colour schemes of its own; the page tint now shades every layer evenly. Web notes greet with the notes changed last when none is open; proposals from the clerk show under its answer; password managers leave passphrases and keys alone.
tabularium.release.0.24.1: The name on the sign-in page is readable with a dark sidebar scheme.
tabularium.release.0.24.2: Passphrases and keys typed on the web pages are shown as dots again (0.24.0 and 0.24.1 showed them as text). Restoring a scheduled backup works with the deployment's own Compose files.
tabularium.release.0.24.3: Tabularius never fetches a web page from a host registered as forbidden among the SSH hosts, in any permission mode, including after a redirect.
tabularium.release.0.24.4: Each web page Tabularius fetches through the server opens its own connection, so a connection left open by an earlier fetch can no longer skip the address check of the permission mode or the forbidden hosts.
tabularium.release.0.24.5: Code for upstream features that Tabularium had already switched off (peer-to-peer sync, the set-up wizard, Setup URIs and QR codes, hidden-file and customisation sync) is removed from the plug-in, along with about a thousand unused messages. A device whose settings still turn those features on keeps them off. The 0.20.0 entry of this history shows its text again.
tabularium.release.0.25.0: The plug-in is about a fifth smaller. Its sync core is now part of Tabularium and keeps only the connection to the Tabularium server; the code for object storage and peer-to-peer sync is gone. A device whose settings still name object storage or peer-to-peer does not try to use them and connects through Tabularium as usual.
tabularium.release.0.26.0: You can pause live sync: "Pause live sync" and "Resume live sync" in the Sync menu of a note or folder, or in the command palette. While paused, edits stay on this device and "Sync now" still sends them. The plug-in now keeps its local data under names of its own, so it can be enabled in the same vault as other sync plug-ins and as Custom File Explorer sorting; after the update, each device fetches its vault from the server once, without signing in again. File sorting now reads an indented list in the body of sortspec.md, with notes after " —— "; rules in the front matter take effect once converted in Settings → File sorting, and until then the file list keeps Obsidian's order.
tabularium.release.0.26.1: Server only: the Tabularius curation rules in a vault's own prompt also change to the list in sortspec.md when the server is upgraded, where they were still as first written. The plug-in is unchanged.
tabularium.release.0.26.2: In reading view, the notes after " —— " in sortspec.md fold behind an info icon after each name: hover to read one, or tap to show it after the name and tap again to hide it. Web notes show sortspec.md the same way.
tabularium.release.0.26.3: Needs Obsidian 1.13 or later. The settings page is laid out like Obsidian's own: the connection first, then a page each for sync, file sorting, Send to Kindle, appearance, maintenance and help, and the search box of Obsidian's settings finds every setting. The sorting note is now Collation.md: a sortspec.md with no Collation.md beside it is no longer read, and Settings → File sorting renames it after a preview, converting rules in its front matter. Web notes, shares and Tabularius use Collation.md as well.
tabularium.release.0.26.4: The file list's context menu has Sorting again: apply or pause sorting, show the item in Collation.md, or move it to the top or the bottom of its folder, which writes the list in Collation.md for you. Several items of one folder move together and keep their order.
tabularium.release.0.26.5: A plug-in folder copied from another vault no longer connects to that vault: its connection is cleared at start.
tabularium.release.0.26.6: Internal restructuring, with no change in use. Style sheets and dependencies follow the community review.
tabularium.release.0.3.0: Connect with a Tabularium login; Send to Kindle; web notes; credentials renew themselves.
tabularium.release.0.4.0: Interface in English, Chinese and Latin; web notes can be edited.
tabularium.release.0.5.0: Tabularius, the AI clerk, answers questions about a vault and proposes changes (0.5 to 0.11).
tabularium.release.1.0.0: First public release. Code, interface and device data no longer use the original plug-in's name; the first start moves this device's data locally, without fetching or signing in again.
tabularium.release.1.0.1: Device values are kept in each vault's own storage. Release files are built and attested by GitHub.
tabularium.release.1.0.2: Code changes from the directory review; no change in use.

tabularium.settings.aboutDesc: Plug-in for a self-hosted Tabularium server. Parts of it derive from code by vorotamoroz under the MIT licence; the notices are in NOTICE.md in the plug-in folder.
tabularium.settings.advancedDesc: Rarely needed. Change them only when the help or a diagnosis points to them.
tabularium.settings.autoLinksDesc: On this device only. About 10 seconds after changes arrive, links with exactly one file of the same name are repaired and logged; the others wait for Check broken links. Turn it on on one device that is usually running: two devices repairing the same notes can conflict.
tabularium.settings.brokenDesc: Looks for notes whose data did not arrive completely and restores them from this device or the server.
tabularium.settings.changeVault: Sign in again or change vault
tabularium.settings.checkLinksDesc: Lists the links that reach no file, for example after a note was moved in a file manager or on another device, and offers the files of the same name as targets.
tabularium.settings.doctorDesc: Looks for settings known to cause problems and offers to correct them.
tabularium.settings.fetch.newer-cleanup: Newer version wins; remove what was deleted on the server
tabularium.settings.fetch.newer-cleanupD: Each note keeps whichever copy was changed last. Notes deleted on the server are deleted here too.
tabularium.settings.fetch.newer-keep: Newer version wins; keep all files here
tabularium.settings.fetch.newer-keepDesc: Each note keeps whichever copy was changed last. Nothing on this device is deleted, so notes deleted on the server come back and are synchronised again.
tabularium.settings.fetch.remote-delete: The server wins; delete files only here
tabularium.settings.fetch.remote-deleteD: This vault becomes exactly what the server has. Files that exist only on this device are deleted.
tabularium.settings.fetch.remote-keep: The server wins; keep files only here
tabularium.settings.fetch.remote-keepDes: Notes on the server replace the copies here. Files already on this device are all kept, which can leave duplicates to tidy up.
tabularium.settings.fetchBody: The plug-in restarts, discards this device's local database and fetches the vault from the server. Choose how the notes on this device are reconciled with the server's.
tabularium.settings.fetchDesc: Rebuilds this device's local database from the server. Use it after a rebuild on the server or when this device is out of step.
tabularium.settings.fetchImpact: Other devices are affected only when notes kept on this device are synchronised to the server again.
tabularium.settings.formatToolbarDesc: Shows the format buttons of web notes over selected text on this device. The Insert submenu (right-click) and the commands stay available.
tabularium.settings.livePausedDesc: Changes stay on this device until you resume live sync or choose Sync now in the Sync menu. Resuming restores the synchronisation settings from before the pause.
tabularium.settings.lockedAccepted: The vault was rebuilt on the server and this device has fetched it. Unlock it once every other device has fetched it too.
tabularium.settings.lockedNotAccepted: The vault was rebuilt on the server. This device must fetch it again before it can synchronise; then the vault can be unlocked.
tabularium.settings.modeDesc: Live: changes are sent and received as they happen. Periodic: every few seconds as set below. On events: when Obsidian starts, a file is saved or opened.
tabularium.settings.needsConnection: Connect to a Tabularium server first.
tabularium.settings.notConnectedDesc: Sign in to a Tabularium server and choose a vault to synchronise this one with.
tabularium.settings.overwrite: Overwrite the server with this device
tabularium.settings.overwriteBody:
The plug-in restarts and uploads this device's files as a new database for the vault. The server keeps the previous database, and the owner can switch back to it on the web.

Without the owner's authorisation for this device the server refuses, and nothing changes.
tabularium.settings.overwriteDesc: Replaces the vault on the server with this device's files. The vault's owner must first authorise this device under Account settings, Vaults and devices, Rebuild vault, on the web.
tabularium.settings.overwriteImpact: The vault is locked afterwards: every other device must fetch it from the server again, and changes on them that were not synchronised are lost.
tabularium.settings.overwriteTitle: Overwrite the vault on the server?
tabularium.settings.reportDesc: Settings, versions and the recent log for asking for help. Passwords, the passphrase and the server address are left out.
tabularium.settings.resetLocalBody: The notes in this vault are not deleted. Until you fetch from the server, this device does not synchronise.
tabularium.settings.resetLocalDesc: Deletes this device's copy of the synchronisation data. The notes themselves stay; fetch from the server afterwards.
tabularium.settings.resolveAll: Resolve all conflicts with the newer version
tabularium.settings.resolveAllDesc: For every note with a conflict, keeps the most recently modified version.
tabularium.settings.resolveAllImpact: The older version of every conflicting note is discarded on all devices; this cannot be undone here.
tabularium.settings.state.live: Connected, changes sync as they happen
tabularium.settings.suspendDesc: Restarts the plug-in with all synchronisation and file watching paused, for when something keeps going wrong. Resume with the command Toggle All Sync.
tabularium.settings.syncIgnoreRegExDesc: Regular expressions on the file path, one per line; matching files are neither sent nor received.
tabularium.settings.syncOnlyRegExDesc: Regular expressions on the file path, one per line. When set, only matching files are synchronised.
tabularium.settings.unlockBody: All devices can synchronise with the vault again.
tabularium.settings.unlockDesc: Ends the lock a rebuild leaves on the vault.
tabularium.settings.unlockImpact: A device that has not fetched the vault since the rebuild may then send old data back to the server.

Firstly, how shall we handle the data retrieved from this remote source?

- **${NEWER_WINS}**: Compares the modified time of files and takes the newer one.

- **${REMOTE_WINS}**: Remote data is the source of truth.
  If you are new to using Tabularium. This option may be easiest to understand and get started with.
  It will overwrite all your local files with the remote data, so please make sure you have a backup if there is any important data in your vault.
